notes: I checked all five fixes against the actual diff and against the current build.py and verify.py. The working tree matches the diff in every hunk.

Fix 1 (only documentary instructions): rubric_words now takes a keyword-only documentary_pages flag that defaults to False, and raises 'supported only for documentary-order instructions' when source_pages appears without it. documentary_order (build.py:1188) is the only caller that passes True. The other callers (unit, segment and fragment rubrics, and citations) get the default, so they reject source_pages before anything is written. expanded_order (build.py:975-977) first validates with rubric_source_pages, then removes source_pages and renders the full text with no pb. This is deliberate and correct, because expanded order has no documentary pagination.

Fix 2 (top scan required): rubric_source_pages uses rubric.get('scan') != pages[0]['scan'] with no truthiness guard, so a missing top-level scan is now rejected. In verify.report, an editorial instruction with witnesses == [], no scan and source_pages now raises from rubric_source_pages instead of getting membership on pages[1:] only.

Fix 3 (printed page tied to the opening page): rubric.get('printed_page') != pages[0].get('printed_page') requires them to be equal, and treats missing and None as the same. The review hash therefore no longer covers an opening label that nothing renders.

Fix 4 (consecutive scans): each scan must be exactly the previous one plus 1. That rules out reversed, duplicate and gapped sequences in one check, and since the step is exactly 1 the scans are also unique.

Fix 5 (verify regression): test_continuing_instruction_requires_review_on_both_source_pages sets reading_keys ['instruction/notice'] on both s12 and s13. Before the review is recorded, 0 pages are complete. With a current review, 2 are complete. After changing source_pages[1].printed_page, 0 are complete again. verify.py:87 requires reading_keys to equal sorted(set(fragments[scan])), so the second page can only reach 2 if s13 now has instruction/notice as a member. Under the old code s13 had no such member and the test would fail.

One function, rubric_source_pages, does the checking for rendering (rubric_words), review hashing (instruction_review_text, which validates before appending the sorted JSON) and verify membership (verify.py:50). Expanded order runs it too.

The rejection tests cover the unsupported caller context, a missing opening scan, a wrong opening label, and duplicate, reversed and gapped scans. The generation test covers mismatched text ('exactly preserve'). Malformed fragments and fewer than two pages are rejected by the validation code. I read that code, but I found no test that targets those two cases.

The synthetic XML has the expected shape: the opening pb (n='a', facs n11) comes before the note, and the note's facs matches it. Inside that one note, a pb with no n (printed_page null) and facs n12 comes before the ' the page' tail, so itertext() gives back exactly 'Example crosses the page'.
The schema check passed: schema_valid true, no errors, one instruction, 2 source-page markers. The test log shows 180 passed and 158 subtests passed.

Two earlier suggestions are still optional and not done: rejecting 'quotations' on a paginated instruction (they are hashed for review but never rendered), and rejecting leading or trailing whitespace in page text.
